boilerplate.section_intro: This section consists of questions and problems involving quantitative reasoning.  Each question is followed by four possible responses.  Choose the correct answer and mark its number in the appropriate place on the answer sheet.

boilerplate.general_comments_title: General Comments about the Quantitative Reasoning Section
general_comments: The figures accompanying some of the problems are provided to help solve the problems, but are not necessarily drawn to scale.  Therefore, do not rely on the figures alone to deduce line length, angle size, and so forth.
If a line in a figure appears to be straight, you may assume that it is in fact a straight line.
When a geometric term (side, radius, area, volume, etc.) appears in a problem, it refers to a term whose value is greater than 0, unless stated otherwise.
When \(\sqrt{a}\) (a > 0) appears in a problem, it refers to the positive root of a.
"0" is neither a positive nor a negative number.

clusters.intro:
Study the graph below, then answer the four questions that follow.

In a certain locality local elections were held.  The residents of the locality who are eligible to vote are divided into two age groups: young people and adults.
The results of the voting are presented in the two graphs below.  The right-hand graph (the darker one) presents the results of the voting among the adults, and the left-hand graph (the lighter one) presents the results of the voting among the young people.
Five lists of candidates ran in the elections: A, B, C, D and E.  In each of the two age groups 200 residents voted, and each of them voted for exactly one list.
Each sector in a graph represents the part of the votes, out of all the votes of the members of the age group, that a certain list received (see key).

For example: 50 young residents and 50 adult residents voted for list B.

Study the table below, then answer the four questions that follow.

Over the course of 20 weeks Tali worked in four jobs: A, B, C and D.
The table below presents data on the hours, the days and the number of weeks in which Tali worked in each one of the jobs.
The background of each cell indicates the job (see key), and the number written in it is the number of weeks in which Tali worked in this job at this time.
A cell that is divided into a number of backgrounds indicates that Tali worked in each one of the jobs the number of weeks written in the part of the cell whose background matches that job, and in the remaining weeks she worked in the other jobs.
An empty cell indicates that Tali did not work at all at this time.

Notes:  Tali began working only at exactly 9:00, 10:00, and so forth.
     Tali never worked in more than one job at the same time.

For example: On day B, between 14:00 and 15:00, Tali worked 17 weeks: 2 weeks in job A and 15 weeks in job B.  In jobs C and D Tali did not work at all at this time.

questions.stem:
Nineteen delegates from 12 different countries participated in a conference.  At least one delegate came from each one of the countries.

At most, how many delegates came from one country?

Given: | x | – x = 6

x = ?

methods.text: For any non-negative \(x\), \(|x|-x\) is 0 — so \(x\) has to be negative before you compute anything. Then \(|x|=-x\) and the equation is \(-2x=6\).
Substitute each option. \(-3\) gives \(3-(-3)=6\) ✓. \(3\) and \(12\) both give 0, and \(-6\) gives 12.

a, b and c are integers that are different from 0.
Given: \(a^b + 1 = 2c\)

Which of the following statements is necessarily true?

methods.text: \(2c\) is even, so \(a^b + 1\) is even, which makes \(a^b\) odd. A power is odd only when its base is odd, so \(a\) is odd.
Nothing at all is fixed about \(b\): \(3^2 + 1 = 10 = 2 \times 5\) ✓ with \(b\) even, and \(3^1 + 1 = 4\) ✓ with \(b\) odd. That kills both options about \(b\).

questions.stem:
A certain car consumes 1 liter of fuel for every 13 kilometers of travel.  The price of one liter of fuel is 6.5 shekels.
Five friends travelled together in this car a distance of 80 kilometers, and divided the cost of the fuel equally among themselves.

How much did each one of them pay (in shekels)?

methods.text: 80 km needs \(\frac{80}{13}\) litres, costing \(\frac{80}{13} \times 6.5 = 40\) shekels. Split five ways that is 8 each.
The 13 cancels against the 6.5 exactly — a sign to leave the division until last rather than computing the litres as a decimal.

questions.stem: How many of the integers between 1 and 30 (inclusive) are divisible by 2 or by 7 (or by both of them)?

With the money that he has, Yaron can buy one book and one pencil.
The price of one book is equal to the price of b pencils.

How many pencils can Yaron buy with the money that he has?

methods.text: His money buys one book plus one pencil, and the book is worth \(b\) pencils. So the money is worth \(b+1\) pencils.
Take \(b=3\): a book costs 3 pencils, so his money equals 4 pencils. Only \(b+1\) gives 4.

questions.stem:
In a box there are 3 balls and 2 dice.
Nurit draws at random, one after the other and without returning, 3 of the items in the box.

What is the probability that the 2 items that remain in the box are the dice?

methods.text: Write both sides in \(x^{1/4}\): \(x^{1/2} = \left(x^{1/4}\right)^2\), so \(t^2 = 2t\) with \(t = x^{1/4}\). Since \(x \neq 0\), \(t = 2\) and \(x = 16\).
Test the options: \(x=16\) gives \(4 = 2 \cdot 2\). One substitution, no algebra.
The target expands to \(xy + y\). The first given says \(xy = x^2 - 1\); the second says \(y = 2 - x^2\). Adding them, the \(x^2\) terms cancel and 1 is left.
Neither \(x\) nor \(y\) is obtainable, and neither is needed. Expanding the target first, so you know which combinations to hunt for, is what makes it work.

Given: 2x + 1 ≤ 0 Which of the following numbers cannot be the value of \(x^2\)?

methods.text: \(2x+1\le0\) gives \(x\le-\frac12\), so \(|x|\ge\frac12\) and \(x^2\ge\frac14\). Any value below \(\frac14\) is unreachable.
Three of the four options are at least \(\frac14\); only \(\frac18\) falls below the floor. Notice that \(\frac14\) itself is reachable, at \(x=-\frac12\), so it is not the answer.

A certain cow produces 4 liters of milk in 8 hours, when no music is played to it.
In the hours in which classical music is played to it, the quantity of milk that it produces decreases by 50%, and in the hours in which pop music is played to it, the quantity of milk that it produces increases by 25%.

How many liters of milk will this cow produce in 8 hours, if during half of the time classical music is played to it, and during \(\frac{1}{4}\) of the remaining time pop music is played to it?

methods.text: The cow's baseline rate is \(\frac48 = 0.5\) litres per hour. Classical hours give half that, pop hours give more; total the hours at their individual rates.
Percentages here modify a rate, not a total, so each hour must be costed separately before adding.

questions.stem:
Given: a + 1 = b
     c + 2 = d

a – b + c – d = ?

methods.text: The givens rearrange to \(a-b = -1\) and \(c-d = -2\). The expression is \((a-b)+(c-d) = -3\).
Pick any values obeying the givens: \(a=1, b=2, c=1, d=3\) gives \(1-2+1-3 = -3\); \(a=5, b=6, c=0, d=2\) gives \(5-6+0-2 = -3\). The answer does not move, because only the two differences matter.
Grouping the four letters into the two given differences avoids ever finding a value for any of them.

questions.stem: \(\dfrac{\left(\left(\sqrt{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^{4}}{2} = ?\)

methods.text: Work outwards: \(\left(\sqrt2\right)^{1/2} = 2^{1/4}\), and raising to the fourth gives \(2\). Dividing by 2 leaves 1.
Every root is a fractional exponent, and the stacked operations just multiply the fractions: \(\frac12 \cdot \frac12 \cdot 4 = 1\).

In a certain hospital the ratio between the number of nurses and the number of head nurses is 3 : 2, and the ratio between the number of head nurses and the number of secretaries is 7 : 4.

What is the ratio between the number of secretaries and the number of nurses?

methods.text: Make the shared quantity match: nurses:head = \(3:2\) and head:sec = \(7:4\). Scaling the first by 7 and the second by 2 gives \(21:14\) and \(14:8\), so nurses:sec = \(21:8\) and sec:nurses = \(8:21\).
Concretely: 21 nurses, 14 head nurses, 8 secretaries satisfies both givens, and the answer reads straight off.

Given: x ≠ y x and y are integers Which of the following equations is not possible?
options: All of the above equations are possible

methods.text: Cubing preserves sign as well as size, so \(x^3 = y^3\) forces \(x = y\) over the reals — impossible when \(x \neq y\). Squares and absolute values lose the sign, so \(x = -y\) satisfies both of those.
\(x=2, y=-2\) satisfies options (1) and (2) at once, which eliminates both and leaves only (3) to check.

questions.stem:
Two medians divide a triangle into 4 shapes that have no common area.

The 4 shapes are –

x, y and z are positive numbers.
Given: x% of (y · z) is equal to y% of \(\dfrac{x}{z}\)

z = ?

methods.text: \(\frac{x}{100}(yz) = \frac{y}{100}\cdot\frac xz\). Both sides carry \(\frac{xy}{100}\), so it reduces to \(z = \frac1z\), giving \(z = 1\) for positive \(z\).
\(x\) and \(y\) cancel completely, which is the signal that the answer is a bare number and that neither letter can be found.

Given: b < 2a 3a < 2b a can be equal to –

methods.text: Every option is a multiple of \(b\), so substitute each into both givens. \(a=\frac{4b}7\): the first needs \(b<\frac{8b}7\) ✓ and the second needs \(\frac{12b}7<2b=\frac{14b}7\) ✓, both true once \(b\) is positive.

Turn the givens into bounds on \(a\): \(b<2a\) gives \(a>\frac b2\), and \(3a<2b\) gives \(a<\frac{2b}3\). So \(\frac b2<a<\frac{2b}3\), and in sevenths that is between \(\frac{3.5b}7\) and \(\frac{4\frac23 b}7\) — only \(\frac{4b}7\) lands inside.
Worth noticing first: \(b\) must be positive, or the range is empty. Chaining the givens gives \(b<2a\) and \(3a<2b\), so \(3b<6a<4b\), which forces \(b>0\).
